chapter: Leaving Hampton and starting his own band
title: First Apollo records of 1947: When I Grow Too Old to Dream and Go, Red, Go
summary: Cobb names the sides cut before the recording ban, including Part One and Two of When I Grow Too Old to Dream with Booty Wood, and a later Jersey date paid on the spot.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: No, well, now, which was the big success out of those first records?
Those records? When I Grow Too Old to Dream, Part One and Part Two.
But he played Blah, da-doo-da-doo-da-doo-dee-doo-da-die, et cetera, oh, da-oh-da-oh-da-oh. That was him on that, and I answered it.
Well, what were some of the others you played there?
Go, Red, Go and Dutch Kitchen -- during that same time. I tell you, we made eight sides before the record band, December the 31st.
You remember that they had a record band that went on in '47. After December the 1st wasn't no more cutting records.
I really don't know because I was in and out of New York, and I know there was black markings in Jersey because --
It wasn't as long as the first one.
-- I'd gone over there to make it, and they pay you on the spot to get it out, you know.
: But it wasn't as long as that first one, was it?
